title: a malformed config field fails open to no restriction at all

provenance.found_by: NorthWoods Sentinel Labs (NWS swarm, run by Margin, for Rob Chuvala)
provenance.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029 (NWS execution-boundary review, round 2, against cortex v6.13.0)

finding: toStringArray returns [] for any non-array value; an empty policy is treated as 'no restriction configured' and calls pass(). CORTEX_PATH_GUARD='{"allowedDirs":"/repo","readOnlyDirs":[]}' (a string where an array is expected) coerces allowedDirs to []. Both arrays empty, so the guard passes every path. A single wrong-typed field silently disables all containment - and it is a config-shape mistake, not an attack, so it can happen by accident.

repros.verbatim: set the env var as above, then Read /etc/passwd - allowed.
repros.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029, finding F2

captured_on.note: Re-established 2026-09-03 on the factory-built VM from the infrastructure factory's first AC-3 run (Vincent Zontini, ProxMox provider, 2026-09-03 UTC) — run receipt: https://github.com/vpzed-dev/smithy/blob/main/evidence/ac-3.md, validated check-by-check at https://github.com/the-metafactory/crucible/issues/27#issuecomment-5520900609. expected: A CORTEX_PATH_GUARD field that IS PRESENT but the wrong shape (e.g. a string where an array of strings is required) must be treated as a genuine failure and DENY, distinct from a field that is legitimately ABSENT (which is a deliberate 'no restriction on this axis' and resolves to []). A malformed value must never be silently coerced into an empty, permissive policy.

fix.summary: validateDirsField now distinguishes ABSENT (ok:true, value:[]) from PRESENT-BUT-WRONG-SHAPE (ok:false, deny) on a per-field basis; parsePathGuardConfig propagates ok:false for either allowedDirs or readOnlyDirs failing validation, and the hook's main() denies rather than silently substituting an empty policy.

verification.note: Unit-imports parsePathGuardConfig and validateDirsField from path-guard.hook.ts and calls parsePathGuardConfig with the finding's own repro string verbatim ('{"allowedDirs":"/repo","readOnlyDirs":[]}'). Asserts ok:false (deny), not a silent empty-policy pass.
